Looking at this problem, I need to find the largest $n$ such that there exists a graph on 2024 vertices (no universal vertex) where every $n$-subset has a common neighbor outside the subset.

## Construction achieving $n = 1011$

Let $G = K_{2024} \setminus M$, where $M$ is a perfect matching (1012 disjoint edges removed). Each vertex has degree $2022$ (adjacent to all except its matching partner), so no universal vertex exists.

For any set $S$ of $n$ vertices, a vertex $v \notin S$ is adjacent to all of $S$ iff $v$ is not the matching partner of any vertex in $S$. Let $P(S)$ be the set of matching partners of vertices in $S$. Then the common neighbors of $S$ outside $S$ are exactly $V \setminus (S \cup P(S))$.

We have $|S \cup P(S)| = 2n - |S \cap P(S)| \leq 2n$. For $n = 1011$: $|S \cup P(S)| \leq 2022 < 2024$, so $V \setminus (S \cup P(S)) \neq \emptyset$. Every 1011-subset has a common neighbor outside. ✓

For $n = 1012$: choose $S$ by taking one vertex from each matching edge. Then $S \cap P(S) = \emptyset$ and $S \cup P(S) = V$, so no common neighbor exists outside $S$. ✗

Thus this construction gives $n = 1011$.

## Upper bound: $n \leq 1011$ for any valid graph

Let $G$ be any graph on 2024 vertices with no universal vertex. I show there always exists a 1012-subset with no common neighbor outside.

**Case 1: $\delta(G) \leq 1011$.** Let $v$ be a vertex of minimum degree $\delta$, with $A = N(v)$, $|A| = \delta$, and $B = V \setminus (\{v\} \cup A)$, $|B| = 2023 - \delta \geq 1012$.

Set $S = A \cup \{v\} \cup X$, where $X \subseteq B$ with $|X| = 1011 - \delta$ (possible since $|B| \geq 1012 > 1011 - \delta$). Then $|S| = 1012$.

Any common neighbor of $S$ must be adjacent to $v$, hence lies in $A$. But $A \subseteq S$, so no vertex outside $S$ is a common neighbor. ✗ for $n = 1012$.

**Case 2: $\delta(G) \geq 1012$.** Consider the complement graph $H$. Then $\delta(H) \geq 1$ (no universal vertex in $G$) and $\Delta(H) \leq 1011$. Since $H$ has no isolated vertices, by the classical theorem (2-color each tree of a spanning forest and take the smaller color class per component), $H$ has a dominating set $D$ with $|D| \leq 2024/2 = 1012$.

Extend $D$ to a set $S$ of size exactly $1012$. Since $S \supseteq D$, every vertex in $V \setminus S$ has an $H$-neighbor in $D \subseteq S$. In $G$, this means every vertex outside $S$ is non-adjacent to at least one vertex in $S$, so no vertex outside $S$ is adjacent to all of $S$. ✗ for $n = 1012$.

In both cases, a 1012-subset with no external common neighbor exists, so $n \leq 1011$.

## Conclusion

The matching construction achieves $n = 1011$, and no graph can achieve $n \geq 1012$. The largest possible value is:

$$\boxed{1011}$$
